title: External & Financial Constraint
text: External & Financial Constraint How reserves, external flows, debt obligations, market access, and the depth of domestic finance shape Argentina's capacity to absorb shocks and finance growth. Argentina's external constraint is not one number. Gross reserves can rise while usable buffers remain thin; a trade surplus can coexist with service and interest outflows; market access can improve while refinancing needs remain large. This area organizes those pieces into a common reading structure, separating stocks from flows and distinguishing temporary financing support from durable improvements in external resilience.

title: Nominal Stabilization
text: Nominal Stabilization How prices, exchange rates, monetary conditions, and expectations interact during Argentina's stabilization process. Nominal stabilization is tracked here through several connected but distinct margins — inflation momentum, the exchange rate and BCRA FX operations, real interest-rate conditions, and the recovery of peso money demand. The active public questions and charts let readers compare those margins without treating any single indicator as a complete measure of stabilization.

title: External position
text: External position Overall relationship between external flows, external liabilities, reserve buffers, and the capacity to meet foreign-currency obligations. Overall relationship between external flows, external liabilities, reserve buffers, and the capacity to meet foreign-currency obligations. core

title: Gross international reserves
text: Gross international reserves The headline stock of reserve assets held by the central bank. Gross reserves are the most visible external-buffer measure, but they should not be read as if every dollar were equally available. Reserve requirements, swaps, repos, and other reserve-related liabilities can make the headline stock diverge substantially from the resources that are readily usable under stress. Headline foreign-currency reserve assets held by the central bank before subtracting reserve-related liabilities and encumbrances. core

title: Net international reserves
text: Net international reserves A net view of reserve buffers after subtracting specified reserve-related liabilities. NIR is useful because it makes explicit that reserve strength depends on both assets and liabilities. The exact definition matters: program measures, accounting measures, and alternative liquid-reserve concepts may differ, so the atlas keeps the measurement convention visible rather than collapsing them into one number. Reserve position after subtracting specified reserve-related liabilities, swaps, and other items under the relevant definition. core

title: Liquid reserve buffers
text: Liquid reserve buffers Reserve resources that are readily usable to absorb balance-of-payments pressure or meet foreign-currency obligations. Reserve resources that are readily usable to absorb balance-of-payments pressure or meet foreign-currency obligations. core

title: Reserve adequacy
text: Reserve adequacy Whether external buffers are large enough relative to the obligations and shocks they may need to absorb. No single adequacy ratio is sufficient. Import coverage, near-term FX debt service, short-term liabilities, and the composition of reserves each answer a different question. The atlas therefore treats adequacy as a family of comparisons rather than a binary judgment. Assessment of reserve buffers relative to imports, external debt service, short-term liabilities, and other external risks. core

title: Reserve accumulation
text: Reserve accumulation Change in usable reserve buffers over time, including the contribution of FX purchases and external financing flows. Change in usable reserve buffers over time, including the contribution of FX purchases and external financing flows. core

title: Current account
text: Current account The balance of goods, services, income, and transfers between Argentina and the rest of the world. A headline current-account balance can hide very different underlying stories. A strong goods surplus may be offset by tourism, other services, or interest payments. Decomposing those pieces helps distinguish a durable export improvement from a temporary compression of imports or a change in financing conditions. Balance of trade in goods and services, primary income, and secondary income with the rest of the world. core

text: Goods trade balance Difference between merchandise exports and imports. Difference between merchandise exports and imports. component

title: Services balance

title: Primary income balance
text: Primary income balance Net cross-border investment income and related income flows, including public-sector interest payments. Net cross-border investment income and related income flows, including public-sector interest payments. component

title: Financial account

title: Foreign direct investment

title: International market access
text: International market access The ability to refinance and raise foreign-currency funding at terms that can be sustained over time. A successful bond issue is evidence of access, but not necessarily of durable access. The broader question is whether multiple issuers can return to markets repeatedly, whether maturities lengthen, and whether spreads fall enough for refinancing to stop depending on exceptional official or secured financing. Ability of sovereign, provincial, corporate, and financial issuers to obtain durable foreign-currency financing at sustainable terms. core

title: Sovereign risk
text: Sovereign risk Market assessment of the probability and severity of losses on sovereign obligations. Market assessment of the probability and severity of losses on sovereign obligations. core

title: Sovereign spreads
text: Sovereign spreads The market premium investors demand to hold Argentine sovereign debt relative to a lower-risk benchmark. Spreads compress a large amount of information into one market price: debt sustainability, policy credibility, global risk appetite, refinancing pressure, and expected recovery values. They are therefore valuable state indicators, but should not be interpreted as a clean measure of any single causal mechanism. Yield premium on Argentine sovereign debt relative to a lower-risk benchmark. measurement

title: External public debt
text: External public debt Public-sector obligations that create material foreign-currency financing needs. Public-sector obligations that create material foreign-currency financing needs. core

title: Foreign-currency debt service
text: Foreign-currency debt service Principal and interest payments that must be met in foreign currency over a defined horizon. Debt-service pressure is fundamentally a timing problem. A country can have a manageable debt ratio and still face a difficult year if large foreign-currency payments arrive before market access or reserve buffers are strong enough. Forward maturity views are therefore central to this area. Principal and interest payments due in foreign currency over a specified horizon. core

title: External refinancing needs
text: External refinancing needs Foreign-currency obligations that need to be rolled over, refinanced, or paid from other external resources. Foreign-currency obligations that need to be rolled over, refinanced, or paid from other external resources. core

title: Official external financing
text: Official external financing Financing from multilateral institutions, foreign official creditors, and other official-sector arrangements. Financing from multilateral institutions, foreign official creditors, and other official-sector arrangements. component

title: Swap and repo financing
text: Swap and repo financing Foreign-currency financing obtained through central-bank swaps, repos, and similar secured facilities. Foreign-currency financing obtained through central-bank swaps, repos, and similar secured facilities. component

title: FX market issuance
text: FX market issuance Foreign-currency borrowing through domestic or international bond and loan markets by public and private issuers. Foreign-currency borrowing through domestic or international bond and loan markets by public and private issuers. component

title: Financial depth
text: Financial depth How much saving and financing the domestic financial system can intermediate relative to the economy. Argentina combines substantial resident wealth with unusually shallow domestic credit and capital markets. That gap matters because a deeper local financial system can reduce dependence on volatile external financing, but rapid credit expansion also creates prudential risks if underwriting and borrower incomes do not keep pace. Scale and diversity of domestic financial intermediation and capital markets relative to the size of the economy. core

title: Private-sector credit
text: Private-sector credit Domestic bank and financial-system lending to households and firms. Credit deepening is potentially growth-enhancing in a financially shallow economy, but the speed and quality of expansion matter. The atlas reads credit growth together with non-performing loans, capitalization, liquidity, and the broader macro-financial environment. Credit extended by the domestic financial system to households and firms. core

title: Credit quality
text: Credit quality Capacity of borrowers to service debt, commonly monitored through arrears, non-performing loans, and provisioning. Capacity of borrowers to service debt, commonly monitored through arrears, non-performing loans, and provisioning. risk

title: Foreign-currency deposits
text: Foreign-currency deposits Deposits denominated in foreign currency within the domestic financial system. Deposits denominated in foreign currency within the domestic financial system. component

title: Domestic capital-market depth
text: Domestic capital-market depth Capacity of local bond and securities markets to mobilize savings and provide financing beyond bank credit. Capacity of local bond and securities markets to mobilize savings and provide financing beyond bank credit. core

title: Domestic savings mobilization
text: Domestic savings mobilization The process of bringing resident savings into domestic financial intermediation and productive investment. Argentina's external financing constraint coexists with a large stock of resident assets held outside the domestic financial system. Mobilizing even part of those savings could deepen credit and capital markets, but doing so sustainably depends on confidence, legal certainty, macro stability, and credible financial institutions. Channeling resident savings, including dollar assets held outside the financial system, into domestic intermediation and investment. mechanism

title: External vulnerability
text: External vulnerability Exposure to abrupt capital-flow reversals, reserve losses, refinancing stress, or external shocks given available buffers and obligations. Exposure to abrupt capital-flow reversals, reserve losses, refinancing stress, or external shocks given available buffers and obligations. core

title: How fast is inflation running now, and is it accelerating or decelerating?
text: How fast is inflation running now, and is it accelerating or decelerating? Separate the current monthly inflation rate from recent momentum and longer-horizon inflation before judging whether the price process is speeding up or slowing down. This page compares monthly headline CPI with three-month annualized momentum, year-over-year inflation, and the month-to-month change in inflation. Reading the horizons together separates the current pace from recent direction and from the slower-moving year-over-year measure. direction_change

title: Has the disinflation process stalled or resumed?
text: Has the disinflation process stalled or resumed? trend_regime

title: How much do exchange-rate movements pass through to domestic prices?
text: How much do exchange-rate movements pass through to domestic prices? Compare official exchange-rate changes with monthly inflation without treating co-movement as a measured pass-through coefficient. The Atlas places monthly changes in the official exchange rate beside monthly headline inflation over a recent window and over the period since December 2023. The comparison is useful for timing and co-movement; it does not by itself identify how much of an inflation move was caused by the exchange rate. mechanism

title: Where is the official exchange rate inside the policy band?
text: Where is the official exchange rate inside the policy band? policy_monitoring

title: How are BCRA FX purchases interacting with the exchange rate and monetary conditions?
text: How are BCRA FX purchases interacting with the exchange rate and monetary conditions? Separate the daily flow of BCRA FX purchases from their cumulative scale and from exchange-rate or monetary outcomes. This page follows daily and cumulative BCRA FX purchases and places them beside the official exchange rate, with monetary-base and money-demand measures linked as broader policy context. Compare the timing and accumulation of purchases with exchange-rate movements without assuming that intervention alone determines the monetary or FX outcome. policy_transmission

title: Are interest rates restrictive in real terms?
text: Are interest rates restrictive in real terms? Compare the nominal TAMAR rate with its ex-post real counterpart before interpreting current rate conditions. The current public evidence compares the TAMAR nominal annual rate with an ex-post real rate constructed using realized inflation. Reading the two together separates the observed nominal return from its realized inflation-adjusted counterpart; the pair is not a complete estimate of expected real policy stance. policy_stance

title: Has short-term interest-rate volatility normalized?
text: Has short-term interest-rate volatility normalized? market_functioning

title: Is domestic money demand recovering?
text: Is domestic money demand recovering? Distinguish genuine recovery in real peso balances from nominal monetary growth that can reflect the price level. The prominent evidence follows the real monetary base and compares nominal with real private transactional M2 since December 2023. Those views separate growth in peso-denominated stocks from inflation-adjusted balances, so nominal expansion is not mistaken for deeper monetization. monetization

title: Is remonetization proceeding fast enough to absorb monetary expansion without reigniting inflation?
text: Is remonetization proceeding fast enough to absorb monetary expansion without reigniting inflation? Read real money balances alongside inflation and the monetary base rather than treating a larger nominal peso stock as successful remonetization. This page compares real private transactional M2 with monthly inflation and places the real monetary base beside real transactional M2. Together the charts keep the recovery of real money balances, the monetary base, and inflation distinct; they do not identify a causal threshold at which monetary expansion would reignite inflation. policy_tradeoff

title: Is monetary-base growth consistent with the monetary-targeting framework?
text: Is monetary-base growth consistent with the monetary-targeting framework? Judge monetary-base growth together with real money-demand proxies and inflation rather than from the nominal base alone. The public evidence is a compact monetization dashboard combining the real monetary base, real private transactional M2, and monthly inflation since December 2023. It places the operational aggregate beside a private money-demand proxy and inflation, but it is not a direct test against an explicit numerical policy target. program_consistency

title: How strong is Argentina's reserve position?
text: How strong is Argentina's reserve position? Separate gross reserves, NIR, liquid buffers, and adequacy ratios before judging external strength. The same reserve headline can imply very different levels of resilience depending on what sits behind it. This question forces the reader to distinguish the accounting stock from net and liquid measures, then compare those buffers with the obligations they may need to cover. state_measurement

title: What is driving changes in reserves?
text: What is driving changes in reserves? Reconcile FX purchases, debt payments, official financing, and other flows with movements in gross and net reserves. Central-bank purchases do not translate one-for-one into reserve accumulation. Debt service, valuation changes, swaps, repos, and other transactions can produce large differences between the flow observed in the FX market and the change in reserve stocks. decomposition

title: Is the current account improving?
text: Is the current account improving? Decompose the current account into goods, services, and income balances rather than relying on the headline total. An improving current account can reflect stronger exports, weaker imports, lower service outflows, or changes in income payments. Those stories have different implications for sustainability, competitiveness, and growth, so the composition matters as much as the total. decomposition

title: Is private credit genuinely deepening?
text: Is private credit genuinely deepening? Track credit relative to GDP and in real terms, not only nominal loan growth. In a high-inflation economy, nominal credit can grow rapidly without meaningfully deepening financial intermediation. Real growth and credit-to-GDP measures provide a cleaner view of whether households and firms are gaining access to a larger domestic financing system. financial_depth

title: What does the rise in dollar deposits mean?
text: What does the rise in dollar deposits mean? Distinguish deeper domestic intermediation from the risks created by foreign-currency balance sheets. More FX deposits can bring resident savings into the domestic system and support financial depth. Their implications depend on how those funds are invested or lent, the currency exposure of borrowers, and the liquidity and capital position of banks. dollarization_finance
